persona: Director of Real Estate & Site Selection, Costco Wholesale — evaluating against Placer.ai True Trade Area and Esri Business Analyst as incumbents
one_line_verdict: A handsome co-location heat-map that tells me where chains already cluster, but it does not yet answer a single site-selection decision — no per-site score, no demographic readout on click, no candidate-comparison, geometric (not observed) catchments, and zero on-map legend to interpret what the dots even mean — so today it is a credibility prop, not a tool I'd put next to Placer.ai.

findings.title: No on-map legend — I cannot tell what T1/T2/T3 or the dot colors mean without leaving the map
findings.evidence: 01-desktop-default.png and 02-metro-zoom-dallas.png show blue/green/orange/red dots with zero legend on the map face; the only tier hint is 'T1 1,021 / T2 1,831 / T3 913' pills in the panel, with no definition. R3 rec.10 flags missing legend; site anatomy confirms 'no on-map legend.'
findings.recommendation: Add a persistent legend in the left panel and on mobile: three swatches labeled 'T1 — strongest co-location / T2 / T3' with a one-line plain-language tier definition, plus a swatch for the retail dots that appear at metro zoom (02 shows red/green/grey dots with no key at all). Until I know what a color means, every dot is noise.

findings.title: Clicking a node gives me rings but no decision data — no population, no spend, no competitor list, no score
findings.evidence: 07-metro-click-node.png shows proximity rings/catchments drawn on click, but no detail panel with the catchment's population, household income, per-capita spend, or who the co-located chains are. Site anatomy: 10,739 catchment-cell JSONs fetched N+1 on click. R2 gap #3: 'no defensible per-site score with drivers.'
findings.recommendation: On click, open a scorecard panel: catchment population + households (you have WorldPop), estimated annual spend (you have multipliers), the list of co-located chains driving the tier, and a single explainable score with its top 3 drivers. This is the literal job — Placer/Esri/SiteZeus all lead with it. Rings without numbers tell me nothing I can underwrite.

findings.title: Catchments are geometric crow-flies rings, not observed trade areas — the credibility gap vs Placer's True Trade Area
findings.evidence: 07-metro-click-node.png shows concentric circular rings (geometric catchments). R2 gap #2 and R1 §6 note catchments are crow-flies/census-spend based; you already hold O-D/mobility data (layer6-mobility-work.pmtiles, MITMA/LODES per artifact registry).
findings.recommendation: Reframe at least the headline catchment toward observed origins or drive-time isochrones. A circle over a river or a freeway with no crossing is exactly the error that gets a site-selection tool dismissed in committee. Even a drive-time isochrone (you have the road network implicitly) beats a circle; an O-D-derived catchment beats both.

findings.title: I cannot compare two candidate locations side by side — there is no shortlist or comparison surface
findings.evidence: Across 01/02/07 there is no pin-to-compare, no shortlist tray, no A/B table. The panel only ever describes one region's aggregate counts. R2 gap #4 (no shareable site report) and #3 (no scorecard).
findings.recommendation: Add a 'compare' tray: let me select 2–4 clusters/sites and render a side-by-side table (population, spend, competitor count, tier, score). Site selection is inherently comparative; without this I'm screenshotting and building the comparison in Excel, which means I'd just use Esri.

findings.title: Heavy overplotting at continental zoom makes the default view read as noise, not signal
findings.evidence: 01-desktop-default.png: thousands of overlapping dots blanket the eastern US into an indistinct mass; 03-region-eu.png is worse — Europe is a solid carpet of dots. R3 recs 5–8 call this out; site anatomy lists 'heavy overplotting at low zoom.'
findings.recommendation: Aggregate at low zoom into proportional cluster symbols sized by sqrt(count), and only explode to individual tier dots past ~z7–9. Add white halos and a circle-sort-key so T1 draws on top. Right now the default screenshot — the first thing an investor or I see — undermines trust because it looks unfinished.

findings.title: 27MB eager payload + 10,739-file N+1 fetch on click reads as a prototype, not a product I'd depend on
findings.evidence: Site anatomy: 27MB eager (clusters-meta.json 19MB + 6.4MB GeoJSON + 1.2MB rm-top400); 10,739 catchment JSONs fetched one-per-click. R1 §1 marks both CRITICAL; 02 shows 'localhost' loading state still visible.
findings.recommendation: Move clusters-meta and archetypes into PMTiles so the client fetches only the viewport; pack the catchment cells into a single tiled/range-request archive with a loading spinner on click. A tool that stalls when I click a candidate site is a tool I stop clicking. This also directly serves the PointSav investor-diligence story.

findings.title: Chain search returns a flat dropdown with no counts, no map context, no 'where are the gaps'
findings.evidence: 04-chain-search.png: typing 'Walmart' yields a plain list (Walmart / Brand / places like Bradford/Eatonville/Concord) with no result counts, no store totals, and the map behind is unchanged continental view.
findings.recommendation: On chain select, fly-to and filter the map to that chain, show '#### locations', and — critically for me — surface white-space: markets with strong co-location demand where this chain (or a Costco) is absent. Void/white-space analysis (R2 gap #5) is the question I actually pay Placer to answer.

findings.title: Mobile is unusable for fieldwork — panel dominates, map is ~40% of viewport, controls overlap
findings.evidence: 06-mobile-default.png: the map occupies the top ~40%, a large WOODFINE GIS panel with tier pills and tabs fills the rest; site anatomy confirms 'zoom buttons overlap' and 'map ~40% viewport.'
findings.recommendation: Make the bottom panel a draggable sheet with collapsed/peek/expanded states so the map can own the screen; fix the zoom-button overlap. My team scouts sites on phones in the field — if I can't pan a trade area on mobile, the tool stays at the desk.

findings.title: Overlay layers stack into an indistinguishable mass with no way to read individual signals
findings.evidence: 05-layers-overlays.png: urban-fringe + commuter + RM-stars all ON produces a dense orange/green/blue field across NA with no legend differentiating the layers and no opacity control visible.
findings.recommendation: Give each overlay its own legend row, a per-layer opacity slider, and mutually distinguishable encodings (don't reuse the tier hues for overlays). Layered context only helps if I can still read each layer; today turning everything on destroys legibility.

findings.title: No data provenance/vintage or methodology visible on the map face — I can't audit what I'd be underwriting against
findings.evidence: 01-default.png footer shows only 'OpenFreeMap / OpenStreetMap / Data Point' microtext; the panel has DATA / DISCLAIMER / METHOD / RESEARCH tabs but no visible 'last updated' or source vintage. R1 §6 and artifact registry note the data-methodology dialog is drafted but provenance isn't a first-class surface.
findings.recommendation: Surface a one-line 'Data: WorldPop 2026, OSM, Kontur CC-BY — updated YYYY-MM' on the map face, and ensure the DATA modal lists every source with vintage. For capital decisions I need to know the population data isn't five years stale before I trust a catchment number.

findings.title: No one-click shareable site report — nothing travels into an investment committee
findings.evidence: No export/PDF affordance anywhere in 01–07. R2 gap #4: Esri's one-click site infographic is the artifact that reaches the IC.
findings.recommendation: Add 'Export site one-pager' per cluster/candidate: branded PDF with the scorecard, catchment map, demographics, and competitor list. This is how a tool becomes sticky — it produces the deliverable my analysts otherwise rebuild by hand.

findings.title: Tier colors use arbitrary hues for ranked data and likely fail contrast on the positron basemap
findings.evidence: 01/02 use blue/green/orange as unordered hues for T1>T2>T3 which is ranked; light dots over near-white positron land. R3 recs 1–4: ordinal data needs an ordered ramp + halos for the 3:1 non-text contrast floor.
findings.recommendation: Switch to an ordered ramp (T1 darkest) or double-encode tier by size, and add white halos so dots clear 3:1 everywhere. Beyond accessibility, an ordered ramp lets me read the hierarchy pre-attentively instead of consulting a (currently absent) legend.

top_priorities: Make a node click answer a decision: open a scorecard with catchment population, spend, the co-located competitor list, and one explainable score with drivers — today rings appear with no numbers, which is the whole job missing.

Add an on-map legend and reframe catchments from crow-flies circles toward observed/drive-time trade areas — without a legend I can't interpret the map, and geometric rings are the exact thing that gets a site-selection tool dismissed vs Placer's True Trade Area.

Add candidate comparison + white-space search and fix the 27MB/N+1 performance — let me shortlist and compare 2–4 sites, find where co-location demand exists but a store is absent, and stop the tool from stalling on click; that combination is what would make me use this over Esri instead of in addition to it.

persona: Tenured professor of GIS & spatial economics — peer reviewer of the implied analytical methodology (co-location clustering, T1/T2/T3 tiering, proximity-ring catchments, regional markets, spend surfaces)
one_line_verdict: The pipeline is competent data engineering wrapped around a spatially under-justified analytical model: crow-flies rings and a fixed half-span radius stand in for accessibility and demand, tiers conflate composition with strength, and not a single uncertainty or provenance signal reaches the map face — a peer reviewer would reject the inferential claims while accepting the data assembly.

findings.title: Crow-flies rings are presented as catchments without any accessibility or behavioral basis
findings.evidence: 07-metro-click-node.png shows clean circular rings around clicked nodes; topic-od-catchment-methodology (artifact A1) defines a 'crow-flies O-D model, 35/150km rings'; R2 gap #2 and #14 flag this directly vs Placer's 'True Trade Area' (placer-ai.png positions the entire product on empirical visitor origins).
findings.recommendation: A circle is a hypothesis about straight-line distance, not a catchment. Retail accessibility is governed by the road network, barriers (rivers, highways, zoning), and competition — a Euclidean ring crossing a freeway or a lake overstates reach by 30-60% in the wrong direction. You already hold LODES/MITMA O-D and mobility data (artifact registry C, Phase 16). Replace or at minimum overlay drive-time isochrones, and where O-D exists, draw the empirical X%-of-origins polygon. If rings must stay for cost reasons, relabel them 'distance bands (straight-line)' — never 'catchment' — and state the assumption on the map face.

findings.title: The ring radius formula (span_km/2 × 1.15) is a geometric artifact with no demand-side meaning
findings.evidence: feedback-ring-radius-policy.md: all tiers use Math.max(1.0, span_km / 2 * 1.15); span_km is the cluster's own internal extent (gis-variable-distance-model.md), not a measured trade area.
findings.recommendation: This makes the catchment radius a function of how spread-out the co-located stores happen to be, plus an unexplained 15% inflation constant and a 1km floor — none of which is tied to population, spend, drive-time, or observed patronage. A reviewer will ask: why would a tighter cluster have a smaller trade area when tight clustering usually signals a denser, higher-draw node? The causality may be inverted. Derive radius (or better, the isochrone band) from a defensible quantity: a distance-decay fit to O-D flows, a fixed drive-time, or a population/spend threshold (radius that captures N households). Document the 1.15 and 1.0km choices or remove them.

findings.title: Tiers conflate co-location composition with co-location 'strength' / market quality
findings.evidence: gis-variable-distance-model.md: 'tier = composition, span_km dist-rank within tier'; UI labels them 'QUALITY TIERS' with 'T1 strongest' (06-mobile-default.png shows 'QUALITY TIERS T1 1,021 / T2 1,831 / T3 913').
findings.recommendation: Counting how many distinct anchor chains share a location is a composition metric, not a quality or strength metric — yet the UI brands it 'QUALITY TIERS' and the cartography research (R3 rec 1) correctly reads it as ordinal strength. A 3-anchor cluster in a dying mall is not higher 'quality' than a 2-anchor cluster in a booming corridor. Either (a) rename to 'Co-location depth (anchor count)' and drop the quality claim, or (b) actually compute a quality/strength score incorporating population, spend, and accessibility (this is also R2 gap #3, the SiteZeus/Esri explainable-score gap). Right now the headline ranking variable is the weakest-justified one.

findings.title: DBSCAN parameters (eps, minPts, IoU merge thresholds) are tuned but their sensitivity is invisible and the choices are undocumented to the viewer
findings.evidence: Two-stage DBSCAN with SPAN_T2_MAX_KM=2.5 gate (phase17-session-state.md); sim-1a/1b/1c threshold sweeps exist (artifact registry Phase 11) showing cluster counts swing massively with parameters (NA: 476 pre-IoU vs 245 post-IoU at P=0.20; IoU=0.10 yields NA=226).
findings.recommendation: Your own sensitivity sims prove the headline cluster count is highly parameter-dependent — the difference between 226 and 476 'markets' is a knob, not a finding. That is exactly what a peer reviewer attacks first. Surface the chosen parameters and a one-line sensitivity statement in the Method modal ('cluster counts vary ±X% across plausible eps/IoU; we report the P=0.20, IoU=0.10 configuration'). Clustering is descriptive, not inferential — do not let the precise count (3,765) imply false precision.

findings.title: Zero uncertainty or confidence is rendered on the map despite 'provisional' framing existing in the drafts
findings.evidence: All ours/*.png show solid, uniform dots and crisp rings with no confidence encoding; topic drafts use 'provisional language' (artifact A1) and regional-markets.json distinguishes high-conf (2,942 of 2,986, artifact C) but the map renders all clusters identically; R1 §6 flags provisional framing as a requirement.
findings.recommendation: Every estimate here — population (WorldPop modelled raster, itself an estimate), spend (proxy multipliers), cluster membership (parameter-dependent), catchment extent (geometric) — carries error, and none of it is shown. You even computed a confidence flag and then discarded it visually. Encode confidence (e.g., dot opacity or a hollow/filled distinction for low-confidence clusters), and add per-estimate error framing in the Method modal. For a capital-allocation and investor audience, rendering point estimates as if they were measurements is the single biggest credibility liability.

findings.title: No data provenance or vintage is visible on the map; OSM/OpenFreeMap attribution is a license obligation, not a nicety
findings.evidence: ours/*.png footers show 'DATA | DISCLAIMER | METHOD | RESEARCH' tabs (06-mobile-default.png) but no source citations or 'last updated' on the map face; R1 §6 and R3 rec 11 both flag this; the text-gis-data-methodology-dialog draft (A4) is staged but the registry shows it DISPATCHED, not shipped to the map.
findings.recommendation: Surface a persistent attribution line (© OpenFreeMap/OSM is required by license; WorldPop, Kontur CC BY 4.0, TIGER, GISCO each need citation with vintage). Add a visible 'data current as of <date>' freshness signal. The Method/Data modals appear to exist as tabs — confirm they are wired and contain the source+vintage+multiplier table, not placeholders. Provenance is the cheapest credibility win and the one most expected of a spatial-economics product.

findings.title: Spend surface chains three layers of estimation (modelled population × proxy per-capita multipliers × H3 reaggregation) with no propagation of that compounding error
findings.evidence: topic-trade-area-data-sources (A2): 'WorldPop 2026 100m raster → H3 res-7 aggregation; per-capita spend multipliers; BLS/StatCan/Eurostat proxies'; layer5-spend.pmtiles is 635MB of derived spend (artifact C).
findings.recommendation: WorldPop is itself a dasymetric model (estimate), per-capita spend from BLS/StatCan/Eurostat are national/regional proxies applied uniformly (ignoring local income heterogeneity — the very thing site selection cares about), and H3 res-7 reaggregation imposes a ~5km² cell that smears intra-cell variation. A reviewer will note the spend layer is an estimate of an estimate of a proxy, presented as a dollar figure. State the assumption (uniform per-capita spend within country/region), flag where local income data would change the answer, and avoid quoting spend to false precision. The MAUP (modifiable areal unit problem) at H3 res-7 should be acknowledged explicitly.

findings.title: Web Mercator distortion is unaddressed while the model quotes distances and areas (35/150km rings, km radii, spend per area)
findings.evidence: MapLibre default Web Mercator (site anatomy); rings specified in km (feedback-ring-radius-policy.md) and the NA/EU dataset spans ~25°-60° latitude (01-desktop-default.png Canada to Mexico; 03-region-eu.png Scandinavia to Mediterranean).
findings.recommendation: A 35km radius drawn as a constant pixel-derived circle in Web Mercator is not 35km on the ground at high latitude — the scale factor at 60°N is ~2x that at 25°N, so Scandinavian rings overstate real distance materially relative to Mexican ones. Confirm rings are computed in a true-distance space (geodesic buffer / turf along a metric CRS) before projection, not as screen circles. If areas/spend-per-area are quoted, compute them in an equal-area projection. State the projection and the distance method in the Method modal.

findings.title: 'Regional Market = any settlement containing ≥1 co-location' is a definition so permissive it undermines the 800/2,986-market headline
findings.evidence: gis-regional-markets.md: 'RM = settlement containing 1..N co-locations'; UI shows '800 MARKETS' and 'Top 400 Highlight' (06-mobile-default.png); regional-markets.json has 2,986 RMs (artifact C).
findings.recommendation: Under this rule a single co-located pair in a small town becomes a 'Regional Market' indistinguishable in kind from a metro with dozens. The term 'market' implies a bounded economic trade area with internal substitution — a definition this threshold does not deliver. Either raise the floor (≥N co-locations, or a population/spend threshold) or rename to 'settlements with co-location presence' and reserve 'market' for a properly bounded unit. The Top-400 cut is presumably doing the real work; make its selection criterion explicit rather than letting the 2,986/800 counts imply more analytical structure than exists.

findings.title: No competing-supply or cannibalization term: the model maps where anchors ARE, never where demand is unmet or saturated
findings.evidence: All ours/*.png render existing store clusters only; R2 gaps #5 (void/white-space) and #6 (cannibalization) flag this as table-stakes for retail LI; the model has no overlap metric despite UI-level merging of overlapping rings (B6, Union-Find groupOverlappingClusters).
findings.recommendation: For site selection, the decision question is 'where is co-location demanded but absent' (white space) and 'how much does a new node steal from existing ones' (cannibalization) — neither is in the model. You already detect ring overlap in the UI (Union-Find merge) but throw the overlap away instead of quantifying it as a competition/cannibalization metric. A reviewer in spatial economics will note the analysis is purely descriptive of current supply with no demand-supply gap inference, which is the actual analytical value retail LI tools sell.

findings.title: Heavy low-zoom overplotting makes the continental view non-analytical — it reads as density noise, not as separable clusters
findings.evidence: 01-desktop-default.png and 05-layers-overlays.png show thousands of overlapping dots across NA at zoom 3.5; R3 rec 5 calls raw points at low zoom 'a legibility failure'; site anatomy confirms 'heavy overplotting at low zoom, no on-map legend'.
findings.recommendation: At country zoom the map cannot communicate any of the tier structure it computed — overlapping dots collapse to a colored smear, so the analytical product is invisible at the default view. Aggregate to proportional cluster symbols at low zoom and explode to individual dots past ~z7 (R3 recs 5-6). Pair with an on-map legend defining what a tier IS in plain language. Without these, the methodology — however sound underneath — cannot be read or audited by the very investor/agent audience it targets.

findings.title: No deep-linkable analytical state — a specific cluster, tier filter, or methodology view cannot be cited or peer-checked
findings.evidence: Site anatomy notes no URL state mention; R1 §5 flags missing deep-linkable map state; the audience explicitly includes 'investor-credibility' where a reproducible/citable view matters.
findings.recommendation: Analytical credibility depends on reproducibility: a reviewer or investor should be able to share a URL that reopens the exact cluster, region, tier filter, and active layers they are discussing. Encode map state (center/zoom/region/chain/tier/layers) in the URL hash. This is also the substrate for the accessible list/table view (R1 §4) that would let the rankings be inspected as data rather than only as dots — the strongest single move toward auditable methodology.

top_priorities: Replace (or honestly relabel) the crow-flies rings and the span/2×1.15 radius with an accessibility/behavioral basis — drive-time isochrones or empirical O-D origin polygons, which you already have the data for. Until then, a circle labelled 'catchment' is the model's central unsupported claim and the first thing a peer reviewer rejects.

Render uncertainty and provenance on the map face: confidence encoding on clusters (you already computed the flag and discarded it), per-estimate error framing for the population/spend proxy chain, required OSM/source attribution, and a data-vintage line. Point estimates shown as measurements is the biggest credibility liability for a capital-allocation audience.

Stop conflating composition with quality: rename 'QUALITY TIERS' to co-location depth OR compute a genuine, explainable strength score (population × spend × accessibility), and surface the DBSCAN parameters + sensitivity (your own sims show counts swing 226–476) so the 3,765 headline is not read as false precision.

one_line_verdict: The basemap choice (positron) is correct, but the thematic overlay violates the two most basic rules of point cartography — it renders thousands of raw, equal-weight categorical dots at country zoom (reading as confetti, not data) and ships no on-map legend — so the map fails to communicate the very co-location hierarchy it exists to show.

findings.title: Catastrophic overplotting at low zoom — the map reads as confetti, not a data layer
findings.evidence: 01-desktop-default.png and 03-region-eu.png: thousands of T1/T2/T3 dots are rendered raw at continental zoom. In the EU view the dots form a solid carpet that fully occludes the positron basemap; in NA the eastern seaboard and Texas triangle are illegible blobs. R3 rec.5 and R1 §2 both flag this as the dominant legibility failure; MapLibre's own large-data guide says thousands of raw points 'become cluttered and difficult to read'.
findings.recommendation: Do not render raw points below ~z7. Pre-aggregate per zoom in the PMTiles pipeline into proportional cluster symbols carrying a count attribute; set the individual-dot layer's minzoom to z7-z9 and source maxzoom ~12. Below threshold show one sized circle per cluster-cell, not 13k dots. This is also the single biggest lever on the 27MB eager payload (R2 gap #1).

findings.title: Tier color is categorical (3 unrelated hues) but the data is ordinal (T1>T2>T3) — wrong visual variable
findings.evidence: 01-desktop-default.png / 03-region-eu.png show T1=blue, T2=green/teal, T3=yellow-gold — three roughly equal-luminance hues with no implied order. The panel chips ('T1 1,821 / T2 1,831 / T3 913') confirm a rank, yet the eye cannot read rank from the map because hue carries no magnitude. R3 recs.1-2: ranked classes require an ordered visual variable (lightness/saturation), not arbitrary hue.
findings.recommendation: Switch to a single- or two-hue sequential ramp where T1 is darkest/most saturated and T3 lightest (e.g. reversed 3-class Blues), so 'darker = stronger co-location' reads pre-attentively. If brand requires distinct hues, adopt the colorblind-safe Okabe-Ito set AND double-encode tier with symbol size so rank survives without the legend.

findings.title: No on-map legend on any desktop view — the audience must guess what blue vs green vs gold means
findings.evidence: 01-desktop-default.png, 03-region-eu.png, 05-layers-overlays.png: the map face carries zero legend. The left panel shows count chips and a 'Regional Markets / Brand / Urban Fringe / Commuter' list, but no swatch-to-definition key mapping dot color to tier meaning, and the overlays (Urban Fringe, Commuter, Top-400 stars) have no rendered key. For a site-selection AND investor-credibility audience this is disqualifying. R3 rec.10; R1 §2 legend check = FAIL.
findings.recommendation: Add a persistent, compact legend in the glass panel: three color swatches with plain-language tier definitions ('T1 — strongest co-location'), plus a nested-circle size key once proportional symbols land, plus a one-line key for each toggled overlay. Make it dynamic — dim T2/T3 rows when only T1 is filtered on.

findings.title: Dots have no halo/stroke — sub-3:1 contrast on positron and indistinguishable where they overlap
findings.evidence: 01-desktop-default.png: the gold/yellow T3 dots wash out against positron's near-white land (#fafafa) and over light terrain; clustered dots merge into amorphous masses with no edge separation. WCAG SC 1.4.11 requires 3:1 for graphical objects; light tier colors fail on white. R3 recs.3-4, rec.18.
findings.recommendation: Add circle-stroke-width 1-1.5 / circle-stroke-color #ffffff to every tier dot (GPU-cheap). The halo both guarantees a local 3:1 boundary regardless of underlying basemap tone and visually separates overlapping dots. Make halo color a function of basemap if a dark mode is added.

findings.title: Inverted visual hierarchy at metro zoom — retail POIs shout, co-location clusters and catchments whisper
findings.evidence: 02-metro-zoom-dallas.png and 07-metro-click-node.png: at z9-10 the dominant ink is a dense scatter of saturated red (and some green) POI dots, while the catchment proximity rings are thin, low-contrast grey circles that recede. The product's thesis (co-location clusters + catchments) is the least salient thing on screen; the supporting POI layer is the loudest. Visual hierarchy should foreground the analytical primitive, not the raw inventory.
findings.recommendation: Demote raw POIs to small muted/low-opacity dots (or cluster them too); promote the co-location cluster symbol and the active catchment ring to the top of the hierarchy with stronger stroke, tier color, and circle-sort-key so T1 draws on top. Reserve the loudest red strictly for the selected node, not the whole POI field.

findings.title: No proportional symbol scaling — every dot is the same size regardless of cluster magnitude
findings.evidence: 01-desktop-default.png: all tier dots render at a single fixed radius, so a 50-store co-location reads identically to a 2-store one; magnitude information is thrown away. R3 recs.6-7: counts/totals are the textbook case for area-proportional (√count) symbols, and radius should be zoom-responsive via a MapLibre interpolate(['zoom']) paint expression rather than fixed.
findings.recommendation: Drive circle-radius by ['interpolate',['linear'],['sqrt',['get','count']],...] bucketed to ~3 discrete sizes (small/medium/large per Axis Maps), wrapped in a zoom interpolation (e.g. base 1.5: z4->2px, z8->4px, z12->7px). This double-encodes tier (color/lightness) and magnitude (size) and keeps small dense markets visible.

findings.title: Overlay stack (urban-fringe + commuter + RM-stars) compounds the clutter with no decluttering or labels
findings.evidence: 05-layers-overlays.png: with overlays ON, additional point/area symbols and star markers pile onto an already-saturated dot field; the result is an undifferentiated mass with no symbol collision management and no label decluttering. There is no progressive/zoom-dependent label visibility — labels (where present) are not managed against the dense symbology.
findings.recommendation: Apply symbol collision (cooperative placement), zoom-dependent label visibility, and per-overlay minzoom so overlays only render where they can be read. Give overlapping translucent areas fill-opacity ~0.12-0.18 with a 1px stroke instead of solid fills (R3 rec.9) so stacked features show through rather than blanket the map.

findings.title: Catchment rings render as undifferentiated thin grey outlines — weak salience and no proximity legibility
findings.evidence: 07-metro-click-node.png: after clicking a node the catchment 'rings' appear as faint grey circles with little fill or tier coding; they neither read as the analytical centerpiece nor communicate which catchment belongs to which tier/center. Combined with the N+1 fetch (R1 §1) the selected-catchment reveal lacks both visual weight and loading feedback.
findings.recommendation: Style the active catchment with a tier-colored 1px stroke + low-opacity tier fill, gated to the active selection/viewport (not all 10,739). Add an optimistic selection/loading state so the click produces immediate visual feedback rather than a silent fetch.

findings.title: Positron basemap is correct, but it is buried by overlays and depends on an external CDN — a credibility-demo risk
findings.evidence: Basemap choice is right per R3 rec.13 (positron is purpose-built for point overlays). But across 01/03/05 the overlay density means the muted basemap's whole advantage — letting data dominate while preserving geographic context — is negated by sheer dot volume. Site anatomy: positron is served from external OpenFreeMap CDN, a single point of failure for an investor-facing map (R1 §1, R3 rec.13).
findings.recommendation: Keep positron as default. Fix the overlay density (findings above) so the basemap context becomes visible again. Self-host/cache the basemap style, glyphs, and sprite so a third-party CDN outage cannot dark the map during a demo. Offer satellite-hybrid and dark as optional toggles (not defaults), bumping dot halos darker on satellite.

findings.title: Web Mercator projection is used while the product quotes area-based catchments — area distortion goes unacknowledged
findings.evidence: All views use MapLibre's default Web Mercator (standard, and fine for the interactive surface). But the product derives census/spend catchments and 35/150km rings; Mercator inflates area with latitude, so a 'ring' or per-area statistic at 60N (e.g. Nordic clusters in 03-region-eu.png) is not geometrically comparable to one at 30N. R1 §2 flags projection-vs-quoted-area explicitly.
findings.recommendation: Keep Web Mercator for rendering, but compute all ring radii and catchment areas in a geodesic/equal-area space (or buffer in metres on the ellipsoid) so the numbers are correct regardless of display latitude, and note the rendering-projection caveat in the methodology/Data modal for the credibility audience.

findings.title: No nested-circle size legend or data-vintage/source line on the map face
findings.evidence: 01/03/05: the map face has no attribution/vintage line and no size legend. R3 rec.11 and R1 §6: on-map basemap attribution (OpenFreeMap/OSM) is a license requirement, and a visible 'data last updated' + source line is a cartographic norm and trust signal. The artifact registry shows a 'text-gis-data-methodology-dialog' draft staged but the map itself carries nothing.
findings.recommendation: Add a persistent small-print attribution line bottom-left (basemap (c) OpenFreeMap/OSM + your data sources + vintage). Once proportional symbols ship, add a concentric-circle size legend (smallest on top, value labels along the tops) — the most panel-space-efficient size key.

top_priorities: Aggregate at low zoom (proportional cluster symbols below ~z7; raw dots only z7+) — fixes the dominant confetti/overplotting failure that makes the continental and EU views unreadable, and is the same lever that cuts the 27MB eager payload.

Re-encode tier as an ordered, colorblind-safe ramp with white halos and ~3 proportional sizes — so co-location rank (T1>T2>T3) and magnitude read pre-attentively from the map instead of requiring guesswork.

Add a persistent on-map legend (tier swatches + plain-language definitions + per-overlay key + nested-circle size key) plus an attribution/data-vintage line — the credibility and usability table-stakes the map currently ships without.

persona: Goldman Sachs TMT banker / IC member evaluating PointSav as the software developer behind gis.woodfinegroup.com — assessing it as a fundable, defensible software asset (differentiation vs hyperscalers, data moat, engineering-quality signals, trust, red flags)
one_line_verdict: Genuinely differentiated dataset and a real product thesis (retail co-location at continental scale), but the front end and delivery architecture read as a talented solo-engineer prototype, not yet a fundable platform — the asset is the data and the co-location model, not the software, and the IC would price it accordingly until the engineering and the moat narrative are hardened.

findings.title: The 27MB eager payload + 10,739-file N+1 catchment fetch is the single biggest credibility killer in technical diligence
findings.evidence: Site anatomy: clusters-meta.json 19MB + archetype GeoJSON 6.4MB + rm-top400 1.2MB loaded eagerly; 10,739 catchment-cell JSON files fetched one-per-click. R1 rubric flags both as CRITICAL. Screenshot 07 shows catchment rings rendering, which is the surface triggering the N+1.
findings.recommendation: This is the line item an IC's technical advisor will lead with. Move clusters-meta and archetypes into PMTiles/vector tiles (viewport-only fetch) and pack the 10,739 catchments into a single tiled/range-request archive. Until this is done, the product cannot be demoed live to an institutional audience without risk of a visible stall — it caps any 'production-ready software' valuation.

findings.title: ~95% of logic inline in one 201KB / 3,659-line index.html signals key-person risk and unmaintainable code — a direct markdown on the software asset
findings.evidence: Site anatomy: MapLibre + PMTiles but ~95% of app logic inline in a single 201KB index.html. R2 gap #15 calls this 'the first thing technical diligence on PointSav-as-software will flag.' No code-splitting, no hashed/cacheable bundles.
findings.recommendation: Extract to modular, hashed, brotli'd, immutable-cached files. Beyond performance, the IC reads a monolithic inline file as 'one person holds this in their head' — it raises integration/diligence cost and depresses the multiple. A modular front end is cheap insurance that materially de-risks the software line of the thesis.

findings.title: The actual moat is the co-location dataset and tiering model — but the UI buries it and never quantifies it, so the defensibility story doesn't land
findings.evidence: Screenshots 01/03 show dense T1/T2/T3 clusters across NA and EU (3,765 NA / 2,728 EU co-location clusters per the panels) — clearly proprietary derived data. But the panel shows only raw tier counts; there is no per-cluster score, no driver explanation, no 'why is this T1.' R2 gaps #3 and #6 (explainable score, cannibalization quantification) are missing.
findings.recommendation: The hyperscaler defense isn't the map (Google/Mapbox win rendering) — it's the curated multi-country co-location corpus and the ranking logic. Surface an explainable per-cluster SCORE with drivers and a visible variable/provenance catalog. An IC funds a proprietary, defensible analytic; it does not fund another MapLibre skin. Right now the moat exists in the pipeline but is invisible in the asset being shown.

findings.title: Catchments are geometric (crow-flies rings), not empirical — the weakest possible framing against Placer.ai for a site-selection buyer
findings.evidence: Screenshot 07 shows concentric proximity rings (geometric catchments). R2 gap #2 and #14: Placer's 'True Trade Area' uses observed visitor origins; the artifact registry shows O-D/mobility data (LODES, MITMA) already ingested. R1 §6 flags methodology disclosure as critical for capital-decision audiences.
findings.recommendation: You already hold the mobility data to reframe catchments toward observed origins / drive-time isochrones. 'Where customers actually come from' is the credibility lever that justifies a premium vs free hyperscaler maps. Geometric rings invite the IC question 'how is this better than drawing a circle in Google My Maps?' — which is fatal to differentiation.

findings.title: Heavy overplotting at low zoom makes the flagship view read as noise, not intelligence
findings.evidence: Screenshot 01 (continental NA, zoom 3.5): thousands of overlapping T1/T2/T3 dots with no aggregation — the eye reads a confetti field. Screenshot 03 (EU) is worse. R3 §B is explicit: 'raw 13k+ dots at country zoom reads as noise'; R3 recommends low-zoom aggregation to proportional symbols.
findings.recommendation: Pre-aggregate to proportional cluster symbols at low zoom and only explode to individual dots past ~z7-9 (R3 rec 5-8). First impression in any pitch is the default continental view; right now it signals 'a lot of dots' rather than 'a defensible, legible intelligence layer.' This is the cheapest perceived-quality win available.

findings.title: No on-map legend — the tier encoding (the entire product thesis) is undocumented to a first-time viewer
findings.evidence: Known observed issue: no on-map legend. Screenshots 01/02/03 confirm no legend; the only tier reference is the small T1/T2/T3 count chips in the left panel. R1 §2 and R3 §C both require a legend adjacent to the map matching rendered colors.
findings.recommendation: Add a persistent on-map legend defining T1/T2/T3 in plain language plus the ring/catchment meaning. An investor or site-selector landing cold cannot decode the map's core claim. For a credibility site this is a trust failure, not just polish — and it is a same-day localhost edit.

findings.title: 3-tier color encoding is categorical hues for ordinal data, and tier colors risk failing 3:1 contrast on the positron basemap
findings.evidence: Screenshots 01/03 use blue/green/yellow-orange dots (unordered hues) for what are ranked tiers; yellow-orange dots wash out against the near-white positron land in screenshot 02. R3 §A: ordinal data needs an ordered ramp; markers need ≥3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11) and white halos on positron.
findings.recommendation: Move to an ordered lightness/size ramp so 'darker/bigger = higher tier' reads pre-attentively, add white halos (circle-stroke), and verify each color hits 3:1. For an institutional audience, accessibility and perceptual correctness are part of the engineering-quality signal — sloppy color encoding undercuts the 'rigorous analytics' claim.

findings.title: Mobile experience is effectively broken — map is ~40% of viewport with overlapping zoom controls
findings.evidence: Screenshot 06 (390x844): the WOODFINE GIS panel/branding consumes the lower ~55% of the screen, the map is compressed to the top, and the zoom-in/zoom-out buttons sit over the map edge. Known observed issue confirms 'mobile panel dominates, zoom buttons overlap.'
findings.recommendation: Implement a proper bottom-sheet (collapsed/partial/expanded) so the map owns the viewport by default. Real-estate principals and partners open links on phones; a demo link that looks broken on mobile is a disproportionate credibility hit relative to the trivial cost. P0 because it directly damages the investor-credibility use case.

findings.title: No trust scaffolding rendered — no visible data provenance, methodology, freshness date, or structured metadata
findings.evidence: Screenshots show DATA / DISCLAIMER / METHOD / RESEARCH affordances exist in the mobile footer (06) but the desktop default (01) surfaces none prominently; site anatomy confirms 'No JSON-LD.' R1 §5/§6: missing JSON-LD (Dataset+Organization), OG tags, last-updated signal. Artifact registry shows a text-gis-data-methodology-dialog draft staged but the panel doesn't foreground it.
findings.recommendation: Foreground a 'Data & Methodology' modal with sources + vintages, a visible 'last updated' date, and add JSON-LD Dataset + Organization(PointSav) markup. For a public credibility asset, citable provenance is what separates 'proprietary intelligence platform' from 'a hobby map.' Cheap, high signal-to-effort, and reinforces the structured-artifact doctrine PointSav already espouses.

findings.title: 404s on metro views are a live functional defect visible during the core drill-down flow
findings.evidence: Known observed issues explicitly list '404s on metro views.' Screenshots 02/07 are the metro/click flows where these would surface. This is the exact path a demo follows: continental view -> zoom to a metro -> click a node.
findings.recommendation: Fix before any external demo. A 404 in the primary investor walkthrough turns a differentiation conversation into a 'is this even finished?' conversation. An IC tolerates roadmap gaps; it does not tolerate broken happy-path navigation in a live asset being raised against.

findings.title: No shareable per-site report / export — the artifact that actually travels into an investment committee is absent
findings.evidence: R2 gap #4: Esri's one-click site infographic; no equivalent export-to-PDF/branded one-pager exists here. Screenshots show interactive panels only, no export affordance. The audience is explicitly stated as including 'investor-credibility story.'
findings.recommendation: Add a one-click branded one-pager per cluster/candidate site. This is the deliverable a CRE analyst forwards and an IC member reads offline — it converts an interactive toy into a decision artifact, and it is itself a strong demo differentiator that compounds the data moat narrative.

findings.title: External basemap dependency (OpenFreeMap) is an uptime/single-point-of-failure the IC will probe
findings.evidence: Site anatomy: basemap is OpenFreeMap 'positron' on an external CDN. R1 §1 flags auditing its TTFB/uptime/CORS and recommends self-hosting for an investor-facing credibility story so a third-party outage cannot dark the map.
findings.recommendation: Self-host the positron tiles/sprites (or vendor a paid SLA basemap). A free community CDN powering the flagship credibility asset is a fair diligence question; self-hosting removes the 'your demo goes dark if a volunteer project does' risk for a modest cost.

top_priorities: Re-architect data delivery (27MB eager load -> PMTiles/viewport tiles; kill the 10,739-file N+1 catchment fetch) AND fix the metro-view 404s — without these the asset cannot be demoed live to an IC without visible failure, which caps any 'production software' valuation.

Make the moat visible and defensible: surface an explainable per-cluster score with drivers + a provenance/variable catalog, and reframe catchments from crow-flies rings toward observed-origin / drive-time trade areas using the mobility data already ingested. This is what converts 'another MapLibre map' into a fundable, hyperscaler-resistant analytic.

De-risk the software itself: extract the monolithic 201KB inline index.html into modular hashed bundles (key-person/maintainability signal) and fix the mobile bottom-sheet so the credibility link doesn't look broken on a phone.

persona: Creative strategist / brand & narrative lead (Madison Avenue — WPP / Wieden+Kennedy school). I judge whether the map SELLS in the first 5 seconds: story, brand presence, the gasp, instant grasp of value, shareability, emotional pull.
one_line_verdict: A genuinely impressive data instrument trapped behind a value-free first impression — it shows me 3,765 dots before it tells me what they mean or why I should feel anything, so it reads as "competent tool," never "must-have insight."

findings.title: The first 5 seconds make no promise — there is no headline, no claim, just a brand and a number
findings.evidence: 01-desktop-default.png: the panel reads 'WOODFINE GIS / LOCATION INTELLIGENCE / 3,765 co-location clusters' — a label and a count, with zero value proposition. Compare Placer ('Market Intelligence For The Physical World'), CARTO ('The Agentic GIS Platform'), Felt ('Make maps, apps, and dashboards in seconds') — every competitor leads with a benefit sentence above the fold.
findings.recommendation: Add one hero line of copy at the top of the panel that states the payoff, not the category. Something like 'Where the right retailers cluster — and where the white space is.' One sentence converts a generic GIS tool into a point of view. This is the single highest-leverage change for selling.

findings.title: The opening shot is a shrug, not a gasp — continental overplotting buries the story under noise
findings.evidence: 01-desktop-default.png and 05-layers-overlays.png: at default zoom the entire eastern US is a confluent blue/green/yellow smear; no single insight pops. R1 rubric §2 flags 'heavy overplotting at low zoom'; R2 gap #1 notes this 'reads as an unfinished prototype.' A gasp needs a focal point; this has none.
findings.recommendation: Engineer a deliberate hero moment: open on a curated, zoomed-to-a-story view (e.g. fly to a flagship T1 metro with a one-line caption 'Dallas–Fort Worth: 1,021 co-location clusters') OR add a glowing top-N 'star' treatment so the eye lands somewhere. Default density should feel like wealth, not clutter — that means giving the eye one place to start.

findings.title: Tier colors carry no meaning to a first-time viewer — the legend that would create the story is missing
findings.evidence: All desktop shots: blue, green, yellow dots dominate the map but the on-map space has no legend (R1 rubric §2 + site anatomy 'no on-map legend'). The panel shows 'QUALITY TIERS T1/T2/T3' as pills but never says what T1 MEANS in plain words. A prospect cannot decode the picture, so the picture cannot sell.
findings.recommendation: Put a plain-language legend on the map itself: 'T1 = strongest co-location (anchor + hardware + grocery)' etc. Name the tiers with words a CRE exec uses, not T1/T2/T3 codes. Meaning is what turns a colored dot into an argument.

findings.title: The metro view's killer feature — proximity catchments — is the actual 'wow', but it's hidden three clicks deep and visually thin
findings.evidence: 07-metro-click-node.png shows the catchment rings on a clicked node — this IS the differentiated story (trade-area intelligence) — yet it only appears after zoom-9 + click, and the rings render as faint outlines competing with OSM road labels. The default view (01) gives no hint this capability exists.
findings.recommendation: Tease the payoff early: an animated 'pulse' on a hero node at load, or a 'See a trade area →' CTA that flies-to and pops the rings automatically. Make the catchment the brand's signature visual — thicker, branded fill, a number on it ('~140k people in 35km'). Lead with your best card, don't bury it.

findings.title: Empirical-origin framing is the credibility story you're not telling — geometric rings undersell real mobility data you already own
findings.evidence: 07 shows crow-flies concentric rings (geometric). R2 gap #2: Placer's entire pitch is 'True Trade Area — where customers ACTUALLY come from,' and the artifact registry confirms you have O-D / LODES / MITMA mobility data. Telling the geometric story when you own the empirical one is leaving the strongest emotional claim on the table.
findings.recommendation: Reframe the catchment narrative around observed movement: 'Built on real commuter and origin-destination flows, not just circles.' Even a single labeled mobility-backed example, captioned, reframes the whole product from 'map of dots' to 'truth about customers.' This is the line that wins an investment committee.

findings.title: Mobile kills the wow — the map is a strip, the panel is the hero, and the story arrives upside-down
findings.evidence: 06-mobile-default.png: map occupies ~40% top strip with zoom buttons overlapping the canvas; the lower 60% is a text panel (WOODFINE GIS / 3,765 / tier pills). Site anatomy confirms 'mobile panel dominates, zoom buttons overlap.' On the device where investors actually open a shared link, the visual product is the smallest thing on screen.
findings.recommendation: Flip the priority on mobile: map ~70% with a hero caption overlay, collapse the panel to a draggable bottom sheet (peek → expand). The shareable artifact must look stunning on a phone first — that is where the link gets opened in the wild.

findings.title: Zero shareability infrastructure — a link to this page renders as a blank/no-preview card, which is fatal for an investor story
findings.evidence: Site anatomy: 'No JSON-LD'; R1 rubric §5 flags missing Open Graph / Twitter Card / og:image as a CRITICAL gap for the investor narrative. A canvas app with no OG image means every Slack/email/deck link is a dead grey rectangle. The map's beauty never survives the share.
findings.recommendation: Add og:title / og:description / a gorgeous static og:image (a styled hero screenshot with the headline burned in) plus a deep-linkable URL state so a specific view is shareable. Shareability is the cheapest growth and credibility lever you have and you currently have none.

findings.title: PointSav, the developer whose credibility this map is supposed to prove, is invisible
findings.evidence: Stated audience includes 'an investor-credibility story for PointSav (the developer),' yet across all seven screenshots the only brand present is 'WOODFINE GIS.' Nothing signals 'this sophisticated engine was built by PointSav.' The diligence story has no author on the page.
findings.recommendation: Add a tasteful 'Engineered by PointSav' signature in the panel footer (where DATA / DISCLAIMER / METHOD already sit) linking to a capability page. The map is the demo; make sure it credits the builder it's meant to sell.

findings.title: The Europe view is the most beautiful, most ownable frame in the deck — and it's a hidden toggle, not the showcase
findings.evidence: 03-region-eu.png: the EU clusters render as a strikingly dense, jewel-like blue/green/yellow constellation over a clean coastline — visually the strongest, most 'wow'-capable image in the entire set. It currently lives behind the 'EUROPE' tab with no framing.
findings.recommendation: Use this frame as a marketing hero / og:image / loading splash. It's proof of breadth ('13 countries, continent-scale coverage') and it's genuinely gorgeous. You already produced the gasp-image; you're just not using it where gasps matter.

findings.title: Search is functional but emotionally flat — typing a chain returns a bare dropdown, not a moment of delight
findings.evidence: 04-chain-search.png: typing 'Walmart' yields a plain RETAILERS/PLACES dropdown list, no result counts, no thumbnail, no 'Walmart appears in 1,402 clusters' hook. R1 §3 calls for result counts and fly-to. The search is the most interactive 'aha' surface and it's the least styled.
findings.recommendation: Make search a selling moment: show a count badge per result ('Walmart — 1,402 co-locations'), fly-to on select with a brief highlight pulse, and surface a one-line insight when a chain is chosen. Turn a lookup into a reveal.

findings.title: No data freshness or scale-of-effort signal — the prospect can't feel how much real work is under the hood
findings.evidence: R1 §6 calls for a 'last updated' freshness signal; none is visible in any panel. The artifact registry shows enormous ingestion effort (50 US states LODES, 13 countries Kontur, dozens of chains) but the UI surfaces only '3,765 clusters' — the depth is invisible, so the value feels thinner than it is.
findings.recommendation: Add a quiet confidence line: 'X chains · Y countries · updated <date>.' Make the scale of the underlying corpus a visible brag. Effort the user can perceive is effort the user will pay for.

top_priorities: Give the map a POINT OF VIEW in the first 5 seconds: a one-line value headline in the panel + a plain-language tier legend + a deliberate hero open (fly-to a flagship metro with a caption) instead of a continental smear of undecoded dots. This is the difference between 'competent tool' and 'I need this.' (P0, mostly S/M effort.)

Lead with the differentiated story you already own — empirical, mobility-backed trade areas — and make the catchment ring the brand's signature visual: surfaced early, branded, labeled with a real number, and reframed as 'where customers actually come from,' not geometric circles. (P0/P1.)

Make it travel: fix mobile so the MAP is the hero (70% canvas, bottom-sheet panel, no overlapping controls), and add OG/Twitter share cards with a gorgeous og:image + deep-linkable URL state — using the stunning Europe frame as the showcase. A beautiful map that can't be shared or doesn't survive a phone never sells anyone. (P0/P1, low effort, high return.)

persona: Senior graphic/visual designer — pure visual craft (typography, color system, spacing, glass panel, contrast, iconography, alignment, polish, desktop+mobile consistency)
one_line_verdict: The shell is clean and restrained — a credible foundation — but the craft is undermined by a categorical-color system fighting ordinal data, dots with no halo separation on a near-white basemap, a missing legend, and a mobile layout where the panel swallows the product; tighten these and it reads as institutional-grade rather than competent-internal-tool.

findings.title: Tier colors are a categorical hue set masquerading as a ranked scale — the core visual-language error
findings.evidence: 01-desktop-default + 06-mobile-default show T1=teal/blue pill, T2=green pill, T3=amber/yellow pill, and the map dots reuse the same unordered hues. R3 §A.1 is explicit: T1/T2/T3 is ranked (ordinal) data, and an arbitrary-hue categorical palette tells the eye 'different kinds of thing,' contradicting the meaning. Competitors who color by magnitude (kepler-demo, carto) use perceptually ordered ramps.
findings.recommendation: Move to a single- or two-hue sequential ramp where T1 is darkest/most saturated and T3 lightest (e.g. dark→light blue), so 'darker = stronger co-location' reads pre-attentively without the legend. If brand recognition demands distinct hues, adopt the Okabe-Ito CVD-safe set (Blue #0072B2 / Orange #E69F00 / Green #009E73) AND double-encode tier with dot size so rank survives. The yellow/amber T3 in particular is near-invisible on positron's near-white land.

findings.title: Dots have no halo/stroke — they bleed into the basemap and into each other, killing contrast and separation
findings.evidence: 01-desktop-default and 03-region-eu: thousands of un-stroked dots dissolve into positron's ~#fafafa land; the amber/yellow tier nearly disappears, and overlapping dots merge into a single smear with no edge. R3 §A.3/§A.18 mandate a white halo because markers are graphical objects needing ≥3:1 (SC 1.4.11) and a halo guarantees a constant local edge over any basemap tone (land/water/parks).
findings.recommendation: Add circle-stroke-width: 1–1.5, circle-stroke-color: #ffffff to every dot layer. One-line, GPU-cheap, fixes contrast everywhere and separates overlapping dots. Make halo color basemap-aware if a dark mode ships later.

findings.title: No on-map legend — the color system is undocumented at the point of use
findings.evidence: Across 01–07 and 06-mobile there is no legend on the map face; the only tier reference is the three pills in the panel header (T1 1,821 / T2 1,831 / T3 913 in 01), which read as counts, not as a key. R1 §2 and R3 §C.10 both flag legend-adjacent-to-map as a baseline. Google/Kepler/CARTO all surface what symbols mean; an investor-credibility map that forces the viewer to guess blue-vs-amber fails the trust bar.
findings.recommendation: Add a compact persistent legend in the left glass panel: three swatches (matching the rendered dot colors EXACTLY) labeled 'T1 — strongest co-location / T2 / T3' with a one-line plain-language tier definition. If proportional sizing is adopted, add a nested-circle size key. Dim legend rows when a tier is filtered off.

findings.title: Mobile layout inverts the value hierarchy — the panel dominates, the map (the product) is demoted to ~40%
findings.evidence: 06-mobile-default: the static info panel (logo, region toggle, search, RETAIL count, three tier pills, Regional Markets, Data/Disclaimer/Method/Research tabs) consumes ~55–60% of a 390×844 viewport, pushing the map up top where Zoom In/Zoom Out buttons crowd the seam. R1 §3 calls for a partial/expanded bottom-sheet, not a fixed block that occludes the map.
findings.recommendation: Convert the mobile panel to a draggable bottom sheet with a peek state (logo + search + tier pills only) that expands on pull-up, giving the map 70–80% by default. Float zoom controls clear of the sheet edge. This is the single biggest mobile credibility fix.

findings.title: Severe overplotting at low zoom reads as visual noise, not data
findings.evidence: 01-desktop-default (continental NA) and 03-region-eu render every individual dot at country zoom; clusters merge into confetti with no discernible structure — the opposite of the precise, authoritative read the audience needs. R3 §B.5–6 and R1 §2 both call for aggregation: render proportional cluster symbols at low zoom and only 'explode' to individual dots past ~z7–9.
findings.recommendation: Aggregate at low zoom into ~3 discrete proportional sizes (scale by √count, area not radius), set the individual-dot layer minzoom so it appears only when dots can be told apart, and add circle-sort-key so T1 draws on top of T2/T3 on overlap. Zoom-responsive radius via an interpolate(['zoom']) paint expression so dots aren't a smear at z4 and pinpricks at z14.

findings.title: Overlay/layers mode produces a muddy, illegible blanket — too many encodings stacked at once
findings.evidence: 05-layers-overlays: with urban-fringe + commuter + RM-stars all ON, the map becomes a wash of overlapping fills, orange RM stars, and the existing dot confetti — no figure/ground, no clear reading order. R3 §B.9 recommends translucent fills (~0.12–0.18 opacity) + thin strokes and gating ring/overlay rendering to the active selection/viewport rather than all-at-once.
findings.recommendation: Lower overlay fill opacity to ~0.12–0.18 with 1px strokes; introduce a clear z-order (basemap < area overlays < dots < selected rings < RM stars); consider making overlays mutually de-emphasize the dots (dim dots when an area layer is on) so only one primary read is foregrounded at a time.

findings.title: Selected-node rings are visually weak relative to the noise they sit in
findings.evidence: 07-metro-click-node: the proximity rings/catchments for the clicked node are thin grey circles that compete with — and lose to — the surrounding dense red/grey retail dots. The selection state, the most important moment in the workflow, lacks emphasis. R1 §3 calls for immediate, unmistakable selection feedback.
findings.recommendation: On selection, dim/desaturate non-selected dots (feature-state), give the selected node a distinct highlight ring + larger marker, and render its catchment with a clearly branded translucent fill + crisp stroke so the catchment dominates its local area. This both clarifies the read and sells the analytical capability.

findings.title: Glass panel is competent but flat — typographic hierarchy and spacing rhythm are under-developed
findings.evidence: 01-desktop-default + 06-mobile: 'WOODFINE GIS / LOCATION INTELLIGENCE' wordmark, region toggle, search, 'RETAIL · NORTH AMERICA' label, the big '3,765' number, tier pills, and Regional Markets all sit at similar visual weight with even gaps; the hero metric (3,765) doesn't command, section labels (RETAIL, QUALITY TIERS, REGIONAL MARKETS) are tiny all-caps that compete with body. Felt and Placer marketing show how much a confident type scale and generous spacing elevate perceived credibility.
findings.recommendation: Establish a deliberate type scale (hero metric ~2× current, clear section eyebrows, consistent label/value pairing), introduce an 8px spacing system with intentional grouping (tighter within a group, looser between groups), and add subtle dividers or section backgrounds so the panel reads as designed tiers, not a stack. Verify glass-panel text contrast (≥4.5:1) over the translucent background.

findings.title: Iconography is sparse and inconsistent — the only icons are the RM star and zoom +/−, with no system
findings.evidence: Across 01–07 the UI is almost icon-free except the orange Regional-Markets star and the zoom +/− glyphs; the Data/Disclaimer/Method/Research tabs (06-mobile) and layer toggles are text-only with no supporting marks, while the search field (04-chain-search) lacks a magnifier affordance. Competitors (placer-ai, carto toolbars) use a coherent icon set to chunk dense controls.
findings.recommendation: Adopt one consistent icon family (single stroke weight, same grid) for search, region, layers, data/method, and the legend; ship a @2x sprite for any custom map markers (R3 §E.16) so marks stay crisp on retina. Icons reduce the all-text density and give the panel scannable anchors.

findings.title: Desktop↔mobile inconsistency: the same panel content is reflowed, not redesigned — alignment and density don't translate
findings.evidence: 01-desktop (left rail) vs 06-mobile (stacked block): tier pills wrap differently, the Regional-Markets row + '800 MARKETS' chip sits awkwardly, and the four bottom tabs are cramped at mobile width — touch targets look under the 44×44 iOS minimum (R1 §3). The two surfaces feel like the same components squeezed, not two intentional layouts.
findings.recommendation: Define explicit responsive rules: which elements collapse, which become the bottom-sheet peek, and a minimum 44×44 target for every interactive control. Keep alignment grids consistent across breakpoints so the brand reads identical in feel at both sizes.

findings.title: Region toggle and tier pills lack a strong, consistent active/inactive visual state
findings.evidence: 01-desktop: 'NORTH AMERICA' is dark-filled and 'EUROPE' is outline — readable but the contrast between states is modest; the tier pills (T1/T2/T3) are always-on colored fills with no obvious pressed/filtered state, so it's unclear they're interactive filters (R1 §3 wants clear active state + zero-result indication).
findings.recommendation: Strengthen the selected-segment treatment (filled + subtle elevation vs ghost/outline for unselected), and give tier pills an explicit toggled-off appearance (desaturated/outline) so filtering reads as a deliberate control. Indicate when a filter yields zero visible results.

top_priorities: Fix the color system: replace the categorical T1/T2/T3 hues with an ordered (sequential or CVD-safe double-encoded) ramp AND add white halos to every dot — together these fix the single biggest credibility read on the map (ordinal data wrongly shown as categories, dots dissolving into the near-white basemap).

Add a real on-map legend that exactly matches the rendered dot colors with plain-language tier definitions — the system is currently undocumented at the point of use, which an investor/site-selection audience reads as unfinished.

Redesign the mobile layout so the map is the hero: convert the dominant fixed panel into a draggable bottom sheet with a peek state (map 70–80% default) and clear 44×44 touch targets, so the product — not the chrome — leads on phones.

persona: Staff front-end engineer (web performance + mapping infrastructure)
one_line_verdict: Engineering-credible cartography wrapped around a prototype-grade delivery layer — a 27MB eager payload, a 10,739-file N+1 fetch, and a 201KB single inline HTML are the three things technical diligence will flag in the first ten minutes, and they undercut the exact investor-credibility story the site exists to tell.

findings.title: 27MB eager payload blocks first interaction and torches Core Web Vitals
findings.evidence: Anatomy fact: ~27MB eager (clusters-meta.json 19MB + archetype GeoJSON 6.4MB + rm-top400 1.2MB). 01-desktop-default.png + 02-metro-zoom-dallas.png show 'DOWNLOADING…' in the panel footer while the whole NA dataset loads regardless of viewport. R1 rubric §1 flags this CRITICAL; LCP/INP targets (2.5s / 200ms) are unreachable while the main thread parses 19MB of JSON.
findings.recommendation: Move clusters-meta + archetype GeoJSON into PMTiles (you already self-serve PMTiles for tiles) so the client downloads only the current viewport. As a fast interim before the tile build lands, split clusters-meta.json by region/tier and fetch only the active region (NA vs EU is already a toggle — load EU's 19MB only when EU is selected). Rough impact: ~27MB → ~1-3MB initial; LCP and INP move from 'poor' to 'needs-improvement/good'.

findings.title: 10,739-file N+1 catchment fetch on every node click
findings.evidence: Anatomy fact: 10,739 catchment-cell JSON files fetched one-per-click. 07-metro-click-node.png shows the proximity rings that appear after a node click — each is sourced from individual files. R1 §1/§3 marks this CRITICAL: it is both an INP killer (request waterfall on the main interaction) and a silent fetch with no loading state.
findings.recommendation: Pack catchment cells into a single PMTiles layer (or a range-request archive / one batched endpoint keyed by cluster id) so a click is one request, not many. Until then, add an optimistic loading state on click (spinner + disabled state) so it doesn't read as frozen, and an in-memory LRU cache to dedupe re-clicks. Rough impact: per-click latency from hundreds of requests to one; INP on the headline interaction back under budget.

findings.title: 95% of app logic inline in a 201KB / 3,659-line index.html
findings.evidence: Anatomy fact: ~95% logic inline in 201KB index.html. R1 §1 marks this FAIL (no code-splitting, ≤50KB chunk target impossible); R2 gap #15 calls it 'the first thing technical diligence on PointSav-as-software will flag.' Inline JS means the entire app re-downloads on any HTML change and is never browser-cached separately.
findings.recommendation: Extract logic to a hashed, brotli'd app.js with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable; keep index.html small and short-cache. Even a single non-split extracted file is a large win for repeat-visit caching and is a trivial localhost edit relative to the payoff. Rough impact: repeat-visit JS transfer ~0 (immutable cache hit); restores any hope of a JS performance budget.

findings.title: No JSON-LD / Open Graph / structured metadata on a credibility site
findings.evidence: Anatomy fact: 'No JSON-LD.' R1 §5 marks this CRITICAL GAP; R2 gap #11 notes it signals professionalism for a public credibility surface. A canvas map gives crawlers almost nothing, and shared links (into an investment committee) render no preview.
findings.recommendation: Add <script type=application/ld+json> with a Dataset (name, description, keywords, publisher=PointSav, license, spatialCoverage) and an Organization block, plus og:title/og:description/og:image (use a static map screenshot). Pair with a crawlable list/table view of rm-top400 — one accessible HTML surface satisfies SEO and a11y at once. Rough impact: shareable previews + indexable content; rich-result CTR lift; cheap, self-contained edit.

findings.title: 404s on metro views degrade trust and indicate broken tile/data paths
findings.evidence: Anatomy fact: 'Known observed issues: 404s on metro views.' R1 §6 requires failed loads to degrade gracefully with a message, not blank/frozen tiles. On an investor-credibility demo a visible 404 or missing layer at a zoomed-in market is a direct credibility hit.
findings.recommendation: Audit the network panel at metro zoom, identify the 404ing assets (likely per-zoom catchment cells or absent tile ranges), and either fix the path generation or guard with graceful fallback + a user-facing 'no data at this zoom' state. Add a global tile/data error handler that surfaces a toast instead of silent gaps. Rough impact: removes the most visible credibility defect; small once the failing URLs are identified.

findings.title: Heavy overplotting at low zoom — the map reads as noise, not insight
findings.evidence: 01-desktop-default.png and 03-region-eu.png show thousands of raw T1/T2/T3 dots at continental/region zoom, fully overlapping. R3 §B is explicit: raw 13k+ points at country zoom is both a legibility failure and a perf cost; MapLibre's own large-data guide says aggregate. Compare google-maps-dallas.png and placer-ai.png, which stay legible via clustering/aggregation.
findings.recommendation: Pre-aggregate per zoom in the tile pipeline: render proportional count symbols (area = sqrt(count), ~3 discrete sizes) at low zoom and only explode to individual dots past z7–z9 via layer minzoom. Add circle-sort-key so T1 draws on top, and a zoom-responsive circle-radius interpolate expression. Rough impact: continental view becomes readable; also feeds the payload fix since aggregation is tile-side.

findings.title: No on-map legend; tier color encoding is categorical for ordinal data
findings.evidence: None of 01–07 show a color legend on the map; the panel exposes T1/T2/T3 pills but no swatch-to-meaning key (R1 §2 requires a legend adjacent to the map). R3 §A: T1/T2/T3 are ranked, so an unordered hue set (the current red/green/blue read in 02/07) contradicts the data's meaning.
findings.recommendation: Add a persistent legend in the left glass panel: three swatches with plain-language tier definitions, updating to reflect active filters. Switch tier colors to an ordered/colorblind-safe encoding (sequential lightness ramp, or Okabe-Ito blue/orange/green) and double-encode tier with dot size so rank is pre-attentive. Rough impact: investors/agents stop guessing what colors mean; satisfies a11y color-independence. Mostly CSS/style-spec edits.

findings.title: Dot contrast fails on positron without halos; color-only tier encoding fails CVD
findings.evidence: Tier dots in 02-metro-zoom-dallas.png sit directly on near-white positron land; R3 §A rec 3/§F: markers are graphical objects needing ≥3:1 (WCAG SC 1.4.11) and light dots fail on white. R1 §4: never encode tier by color alone.
findings.recommendation: Add circle-stroke-width 1–1.5 / circle-stroke-color #fff (a one-line style change) so every dot keeps a constant 3:1 local boundary regardless of basemap feature underneath; pair color with size/label (from the legend fix) for color-independence. Rough impact: fixes contrast across the whole map in one paint property; removes the single biggest a11y failure mode for this map type.

findings.title: Canvas map + glass panels have no keyboard/screen-reader path
findings.evidence: R1 §4: canvas MapLibre is typically a keyboard black hole; needs role=region + aria-label, aria-live for selection/zoom/result-count changes, and a text/table alternative. Nothing in the markup facts indicates this exists, and 04-chain-search.png shows a results dropdown with no visible result counts or empty-state affordance.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the map in role=region with a descriptive aria-label; add an aria-live=polite region announcing selection/zoom/result counts; ship the rm-top400 list/table as the non-visual alternative (doubles as the SEO crawlable surface). Add result counts + no-match messaging to search. Rough impact: makes the product operable without a mouse and indexable; the list view is reusable across a11y + SEO findings.

findings.title: Mobile panel dominates viewport; zoom controls overlap
findings.evidence: 06-mobile-default.png: the panel (title, tiers, regional-markets, layers, footer links) occupies ~60% of the screen with the map compressed to the top ~40%; zoom +/- buttons sit near the panel edge. R1 §3 requires a drawer/sheet that doesn't occlude the map and ≥24×24 (aim 44×44) touch targets.
findings.recommendation: Convert the mobile panel to a bottom sheet with collapsed/peek/expanded states (map default ~70%+); reposition zoom controls clear of the sheet; verify tier pills and toggles meet 44×44. Rough impact: map becomes the hero on mobile; controls stop colliding; pure layout/CSS work on localhost.

findings.title: Basemap on external OpenFreeMap CDN is a single point of failure for the demo
findings.evidence: Anatomy fact: basemap positron on external CDN (OpenFreeMap); footer in 01-desktop-default.png shows the OpenFreeMap/OpenStreetMap attribution. R1 §1/R3 §D: for an investor-facing product a third-party outage or latency spike can dark the map mid-demo, and you already self-host PMTiles.
findings.recommendation: Self-host (or cache via your own CDN) the style JSON, glyphs, and sprite at minimum — you already self-serve PMTiles, so the basemap is the only external dependency on the critical path. Keep positron as the default (correct choice for point overlays per R3 §D). Rough impact: removes the only third-party critical-path dependency; insulates the credibility demo from an outage.

findings.title: No deep-linkable URL state — views aren't shareable or bookmarkable
findings.evidence: R1 §5 requires center/zoom/region/chain/tier/layers encoded in the URL. Across 02 (Dallas), 03 (EU), 04 (Walmart search), 05 (overlays on) the app changes state with no indication it's reflected in a shareable URL — yet the audience explicitly includes sending a view into an investor deck (R2 gap #9, Felt's frictionless share).
findings.recommendation: Serialize map state (center/zoom, NA|EU, selected chain, active tiers, layer toggles) into URL hash/query params and restore on load. Rough impact: any specific market/chain view becomes a copy-paste link for a deck or a colleague; low effort, high narrative value; self-contained JS change.

top_priorities: Kill the eager-load + N+1 trio: move clusters-meta and archetypes into viewport-only PMTiles (interim: split by region and load EU only on toggle) and pack the 10,739 catchment cells into a single tiled/batched source with a click loading state. This is the dominant perf problem and the #1 technical-diligence credibility risk.

Extract the inline JS to a hashed, brotli'd, immutable-cached app.js and add JSON-LD (Dataset + Organization) + OG tags + a crawlable rm-top400 list/table view — three cheap-to-moderate edits that fix caching, SEO, shareability, and the screen-reader/non-visual alternative in one pass.

Cartographic legibility pass: low-zoom aggregation to stop overplotting, white dot halos for 3:1 contrast, an on-map tier legend with ordered/CVD-safe colors double-encoded by size, and a mobile bottom-sheet so the map is the hero — the visible-quality fixes that make the map read as insight rather than noise.

persona: Principal UI/UX Designer — interaction & flows specialist (onboarding, search/discovery, selection/inspector, proximity-ring interaction, loading/empty states, mobile)
one_line_verdict: The data and cartographic ambition are real, but the interaction layer reads as an un-onboarded power tool: no first-run orientation, no legend, a selection model that fires a silent 10,739-file fetch, and a mobile layout where the panel eats the map — each a recognized heuristic failure that undercuts both the site-selection job and the investor-credibility story.

findings.title: Mobile: the panel dominates the viewport and buries the primary object (the map)
findings.evidence: 06-mobile-default.png — map occupies the top ~40% and the WOODFINE GIS / search / quality-tiers / Regional Markets / Retail panel consumes the lower ~60%; zoom +/- buttons sit at the map's bottom edge where they overlap the panel header. Stated fact: 'mobile panel dominates; map ~40% viewport, zoom buttons overlap.'
findings.recommendation: Convert the mobile panel to a 3-state bottom sheet (peek ~15% showing search + tier counts / half ~50% / full) with a drag handle, defaulting to PEEK so the map is the hero on load. Move zoom controls to the upper-right of the map and ensure they never sit under the sheet. This restores Nielsen heuristic #8 (aesthetic/minimalist — content prioritized) and #6 (recognition: the map IS the product). Mirrors Google Maps Dallas (google-maps-dallas.png) where chrome is a thin top bar + corner controls and the map is ~95% of the frame.

findings.title: No first-run orientation — user is dropped into a continental dot-storm with no 'what am I looking at / what do I do'
findings.evidence: 01-desktop-default.png shows thousands of blue/green/yellow dots over NA at zoom 3.5 with the panel showing only raw counts (3,765 clusters; T1/T2/T3 chips). There is no caption, no callout, no empty-to-action cue explaining tiers, rings, or the search-first path. Contrast Placer.ai (placer-ai.png) and Felt (felt.png) which lead with a single clear value line + one obvious action.
findings.recommendation: Add a dismissible first-run overlay (or inline coachmarks) with 3 beats: (1) one sentence defining a co-location cluster + what T1/T2/T3 mean; (2) 'Search a city/chain or click a dot to inspect its catchment'; (3) a 'Take a tour' / 'Skip' pair. Persist dismissal in localStorage. This addresses heuristic #10 (help & documentation) and #6 (recognition over recall). For the investor audience, the first 5 seconds currently read as raw output, not a product.

findings.title: Cluster selection fires a silent N+1 catchment fetch with no loading or selected state
findings.evidence: Fact: 'proximity rings = catchments; 10,739 catchment-cell JSON files fetched N+1 on click; 404s on metro views.' 07-metro-click-node.png shows rings appear but no visible selection highlight on the clicked node, no spinner, no panel transition. R1 rubric §3 flags this explicitly: 'never a silent 10,739-file fetch with no spinner.'
findings.recommendation: On click: (1) immediately apply a selected-state ring/halo to the node (optimistic, 0ms via feature-state); (2) show a skeleton/loading shimmer in the inspector while catchment cells resolve; (3) batch the fetch (single PMTiles/range-request archive) so it returns in one round-trip; (4) render a graceful inline error if cells 404 instead of leaving rings half-drawn. Heuristics #1 (visibility of system status) and #9 (error recovery). Until the data is tiled, even a single aggregated request + spinner removes the 'is it broken?' feeling.

findings.title: No on-map legend — color tier and ring meaning are unguessable
