findings.evidence: 01/02/03/05 — no legend appears anywhere in the panel or map face; tier chips (T1/T2/T3) are colored counts but never paired with a 'what the dot color means' key, and rings (07) have no explanation. R3 cartography §10–11 and stated fact 'no on-map legend.' R3 also notes T1/T2/T3 is ordinal data wrongly encoded as unordered hues, making a legend doubly necessary.
findings.recommendation: Add a persistent compact legend in the panel/map corner: three swatches labelled 'T1 — strongest co-location / T2 / T3' with a one-line tier definition, plus a 'proximity ring = modelled catchment (crow-flies)' note. Make it filter-reactive (dim T2/T3 rows when only T1 is on). Heuristics #2 (match to real world via plain language) and #6 (recognition). This is the cheapest credibility win on the board.

findings.title: Search is the intended primary path but is visually demoted and lacks discovery feedback
findings.evidence: 04-chain-search.png — typing 'Walmart' yields a dropdown split into 'PLACES' and an unlabeled list (Walmart / Bradford?/Concord?) with no result counts, no chain-vs-place distinction icons, and no 'X stores found' summary. The search field is a thin secondary row under the brand lockup rather than the hero action that Placer.ai (placer-ai.png) and the rubric §3 prescribe.
findings.recommendation: Promote search to the top of the panel with placeholder 'Search a chain, city, or retailer', add section headers with counts ('Chains (3)', 'Places (12)'), distinct icons for chain vs place, debounce + keyboard nav (arrow/Enter), a clear (x) affordance, and a no-match empty message ('No chain matches "xyz" — try a city'). On select, fly-to with an aria-live announcement. Heuristics #1, #6, and §3 search/discovery in the rubric.

findings.title: Heavy overplotting at low zoom makes the default view read as noise, not insight
findings.evidence: 01-desktop-default.png and 02-metro-zoom-dallas.png — at zoom 3.5 thousands of dots merge into solid masses over the US Northeast/Texas; at the Dallas metro the red retail dots + cluster dots overplot heavily. Fact: 'heavy overplotting at low zoom.' R3 §5–9 prescribes aggregation. Google's same-metro view (google-maps-dallas.png) stays legible by progressive labeling and decluttering.
findings.recommendation: Aggregate to proportional count-symbols at low zoom (√count, ~3 discrete sizes) and only explode to individual dots past ~z7–z9 via layer minzoom; add white halos (R3 §3) and circle-sort-key so T1 draws on top. Add a low-zoom cue 'Zoom in to see individual locations.' This is both a legibility and a perceived-performance fix. Heuristic #8 (minimalist — show the signal, hide the noise until it's resolvable).

findings.title: Layers/overlays produce visual overload with no per-layer control state or count feedback
findings.evidence: 05-layers-overlays.png — with urban-fringe + commuter + RM-stars all ON, the map becomes an unreadable wash of orange/blue/green; the LAYERS list (Urban Fringe / Commuter / RM stars) shows toggles but no active-emphasis, no 'N features', and no warning that combining them defeats legibility. R1 §3 filters guidance: toggles should show active state and indicate zero/over results.
findings.recommendation: Give each toggle a clear on/off visual (filled vs outline), a per-layer count or 'visible at this zoom' hint, and consider mutually-exclusive grouping or an opacity slider for dense overlays. Add a 'Reset layers' affordance. When a layer has no features in view, gray it with 'none in view'. Heuristics #3 (user control/freedom) and #1 (status).

findings.title: Inspector/bento has no per-cluster scorecard — selection reveals a catchment but not a decision
findings.evidence: 07-metro-click-node.png shows rings drawn but the left panel does not transition into a detailed inspector with the cluster's tier, member chains, population/spend in catchment, or a rank. R2 teardown gap #3: 'You show tiers but no defensible per-site score with drivers' — the artifact every site-selection/investor audience buys.
findings.recommendation: On selection, swap the panel to a bento inspector: header (cluster name + tier badge), key stats (member chains as logos/chips, catchment population, est. spend, rank within region), and a 'Why this tier' one-liner. Provide a back affordance to the overview. This turns a polygon into a decision and directly serves the credibility narrative. Heuristic #2 (real-world relevance) + competitive parity with Placer/SiteZeus.

findings.title: Loading state for the 27MB eager payload is invisible — first paint risks a frozen-looking map
findings.evidence: Fact: 'eager payload ~27MB (clusters-meta.json 19MB + archetype 6.4MB + rm-top400 1.2MB).' R1 §1/§3 flags INP risk parsing 19MB JSON and prescribes 'a skeleton or progress indicator so the map doesn't appear frozen.' No screenshot shows a loading affordance.
findings.recommendation: Add a lightweight load sequence: render the basemap + panel chrome first, show a 'Loading 3,765 clusters…' progress chip, and stream/paginate the dot layer so the user sees motion within ~1s. Pair with the longer-term PMTiles migration (R1 priority #1) so the 27MB drops to viewport-only. Heuristic #1 (visibility of system status). Investors notice a hang on the first demo click.

findings.title: Empty/error states are unhandled — 404s on metro views degrade silently
findings.evidence: Fact: '404s on metro views.' 02-metro-zoom-dallas.png is dense but there is no surfaced messaging when catchment cells fail; R1 §3/§6 require empty/loading/error states for every async surface and graceful basemap-CDN-failure handling (positron is external/OpenFreeMap).
findings.recommendation: Add explicit states: (a) catchment 404 → inline 'Catchment data unavailable for this cluster'; (b) zero search results → friendly empty copy with a suggestion; (c) basemap CDN unreachable → 'Basemap temporarily unavailable' banner instead of a blank/gray canvas. Heuristic #9 (help users recognize/recover from errors). Self-hosting basemap sprites/glyphs (R3 §13) removes one credibility-risking single point of failure.

findings.title: No shareable/deep-linkable view state — breaks the investor 'send a link' flow
findings.evidence: No URL/state affordance is visible across screenshots; R1 §5 prescribes 'deep-linkable map state in the URL (center/zoom/region/chain/tier/layers)' and R2 gap #9 highlights Felt's frictionless link-share as the investor-deck pattern. The NA/EU toggle (01 vs 03) and selected chain (04) currently have no shareable representation.
findings.recommendation: Encode center/zoom, region (NA/EU), active chain, tier filters, and active layers in the URL hash so any view is bookmarkable and shareable. Add a 'Copy link to this view' button in the panel. Low effort, high narrative value (heuristic #7 flexibility/efficiency; supports the credibility story directly).

findings.title: Touch targets and control affordances under-sized / ambiguous at mobile width
findings.evidence: 06-mobile-default.png — the colored tier dots, the DATA/DISCLAIMER/METHOD/RESEARCH footer links, and the zoom controls are small and tightly packed near the sheet edge. R1 §3 requires ≥24×24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), target 44×44 iOS. Tier dots and packed footer links are likely below target.
findings.recommendation: Enforce ≥44×44px hit areas on all tappable controls (dots get an invisible padded hit area; footer links get vertical spacing; zoom buttons enlarged and repositioned). Add visible focus rings (≥3:1). This is both an accessibility and a fat-finger usability fix; pairs naturally with the bottom-sheet rework. Heuristic-adjacent: error prevention (#5) via larger targets.

top_priorities: Fix mobile layout: convert the panel to a 3-state bottom sheet defaulting to PEEK so the map is the hero, and reposition zoom controls out from under it (06-mobile-default.png) — the panel-dominates problem currently makes the product unusable on the device most investors will open the link on.

Make selection trustworthy: add an instant selected-state + inspector skeleton on cluster click, batch the 10,739-file catchment fetch into one request, and handle 404s gracefully (07-metro-click-node.png) — today a click triggers a silent fetch storm that reads as broken.

Orient the first-time user: add a dismissible first-run overlay defining tiers/rings + the search-first path AND a persistent on-map legend (01-desktop-default.png has neither) — the cheapest, highest-leverage fixes for both the site-selection job and the investor-credibility story.
